_comment: UTAH STATE LEGISLATURE — printed vote-page name → PolitiDex roster id, for the 2024 General Session. Keys are the EXACT string le.utah.gov prints on a vote page. Same discipline as db/vr-utah-member-map.json (2025GS): resolution is by NAME against a per-chamber candidate pool and the district only ever CONFIRMS, never resolves, because a district's occupant changes between sessions. `unmapped` is people who cast recorded votes in these roll calls and are not on the PolitiDex roster — their votes are dropped, counted and disclosed, never handed to whoever holds the seat now.
_howReviewed: scripts/vr-utah-ingest.mjs --collect --session 2024GS proposed 55 House and 27 Senate names and left 22 for review. Every proposal was then checked against a source the ingest does not read: the legislature's own roster for that year, https://le.utah.gov/asp/roster/roster.asp?year=2024, which prints full name, chamber and district for the 105 people who actually served in 2024. Each accepted printed name appears in that roster in the SAME chamber as the roll call, and the roster's full name agrees with the roster id it was mapped to. That check is what rules out the successor error: a 2024 member who has since left prints no district on the vote page, so a namesake now serving would otherwise be indistinguishable. Six accepted names carry no district on the vote page (Bennion, Burton, Clancy, Gwynn, Moss C., Thatcher in the Senate) and rest on full-name agreement with the 2024 roster instead.
_collisionsThatUsedToBeRefused: The 2025 map refused "Moss, J.", "Peterson, K." and "Peterson, T." because the roster carried only one Moss and one Peterson and a guess would have invented a stranger. Wave 2's roster additions ended that: in 2024 the House seated Carol S. Moss (34) and Jefferson Moss (51), and Karen M. Peterson (13), Thomas W. Peterson (1) and Val L. Peterson (56), and all five are on the roster under their own ids. The printed forms are distinct — "Moss, C." / "Moss, J.", "Peterson, K." / "Peterson, T." / "Peterson, V." — so each resolves on its own initial, confirmed against the 2024 roster. Nothing here rests on a surname alone.
_crossChamberNotes: Three printed names are 2024 House members whose roster record is a Utah STATE SENATE seat, because they moved chambers afterwards: "Brammer, B." (House 54 in 2024) is Brady Brammer, now Senate 21; "Musselman, C.R." (House 9) is Calvin Musselman, now Senate 4; "Stratton, K." (House 58) is Keven Stratton, now Senate 24. The ingest's candidate pool is filtered by CURRENT office, so it proposed none of them; each was added here by hand. What is being asserted is identity of the person, not of the seat: the surname is unique across all 784 roster entries, the first name agrees with the 2024 roster, and the roll call itself carries the chamber, so a 2024 Utah House vote stays a Utah House vote no matter which chamber the member sits in now. "Walter, N." is the same case the 2025 map already accepted — R. Neil Walter, House 74, who goes by his middle name — and here the vote page printed the district too.
_refusalNotes: Two printed names match a roster entry with the same distinctive name whose office is NOT a Utah legislative seat: "Judkins, M." (Marsha Judkins, House 61 in 2024) against a roster record for a Marsha Judkins who is Mayor of Provo, and "Lyman, P." (Phil Lyman, House 69) against a roster record for a Phil Lyman who is a candidate for governor. Both are probably the same human, and probably is the wrong standard for handing one person's votes to another person's page. Neither prints a district on the vote page — they had left the legislature by the time the page was served — so there is no second key to confirm with, and a mayoral or statewide-candidate record is not evidence of a legislative career. Both stay unattributed. A source that establishes the identity would settle it; guessing would not.
_federalMoveNotes: "Kennedy, M." is Michael S. Kennedy, Utah Senate 21 in 2024, who is now a U.S. Representative. The roster carries him as a federal member and federal ingest is out of scope for this wave, so his 2024 state votes are dropped rather than filed onto a congressional record. That is a deliberate coverage gap, not a resolution failure.
_unmappedIsCoverage: Everyone left in `unmapped` served in 2024 and is not on the PolitiDex roster at all — most left the legislature before the roster snapshot was taken. Their votes are counted and disclosed by the migration and by scripts/test-vr-utah-record.mjs, and attributed to nobody. Adding them is a roster decision for a later wave, made from a source, not something the ingest may infer from a vote page.
